==English== ===Pronunciation=== * {{enPR|chäm|a=RP}}, {{IPA|en|/tʃɑːm/}} * {{enPR|chärm|a=GA}}, {{IPA|en|/t͡ʃɑɹm/}} ** {{audio|en|En-us-charm.ogg|a=US}} * {{rhymes|en|ɑː(ɹ)m|s=1}} ===Etymology 1=== From {{inh|en|enm|charme}}, from {{der|en|fro|charme||chant, magic spell}}, from {{der|en|la|carmen||song, incantation}}. Displaced native {{noncog|ang|lybb||drug, poison, charm}}. ====Alternative forms==== * {{alter|en|charme||obsolete}} ====Noun==== {{en-noun|~}} # An object, act or words believed to have [[magic]] [[power]] (usually carries a positive connotation). #: {{syn|en|incantation|spell|talisman|Thesaurus:amulet|Thesaurus:magic spell}} #: {{ux|en|a '''charm''' against evil}} #: {{ux|en|It works [[like a charm|like a '''charm''']].}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1961|author={{w|Harry E. Wedeck}}|title=Dictionary of Aphrodisiacs|publisher=The Citadel Press|location=New York|page=223|passage=The witch, repository of hieratic lore and folk legends and occult arcana, became the distributor of philtres and unguents, electuaries and pastilles, herbs and '''charms''' and incantations - directed toward sexual pleasures and amatory satisfactions.}} # {{lb|en|often|in plural}} The ability to [[persuade]], [[delight]] or arouse [[admiration]]. #: {{syn|en|appeal|attraction|charisma}} #: {{ant|en|boredom|dryness}} #: {{ux|en|He had great personal '''charm'''.}} #: {{ux|en|She tried to win him over with her '''charms'''.}} #* {{RQ:Milton Paradise Lost|book=VIII|page=248|passage={{...}}the '''charm''' of Beauties powerful glance.|year=1873}} #* {{RQ:Congreve Mourning Bride|page=1|passage=Muſick has '''Charms''' to ſooth a ſavage Breaſt,
To ſoften Rocks, or bend a knotted Oak.}} #* {{RQ:Pope Rape of the Lock|year=1717|canto=V|page=160|passage='''Charms''' ſtrike the ſight, but merit wins the ſoul.}} #* {{quote-book|en|year=1769|author={{w|Firishta}}|tlr={{w|Alexander Dow}}|title=Tales translated from the Persian of Inatulla of Delhi|volume=I|publisher=P. and W. Wilson et al.|location=Dublin|page=15|text=Her coyneſs was conquered by aſſiduity, and at laſt ſhe conſented to reſign the treaſure of her '''charms''' to my paſſion.}} # A small [[trinket]] on a [[bracelet]] or chain, etc., traditionally supposed to confer [[luck]] upon the wearer. #: {{syn|en|amulet|dangle|ornament|Thesaurus:amulet}} #: {{ux|en|She wears a [[charm bracelet|'''charm''' bracelet]] on her wrist.}} # {{lb|en|collective}} A group of [[goldfinch]]es or other [[songbird]]s, or sometimes [[hummingbird]]s. #: {{syn|en|flock}} # {{lb|en|particle physics}} A [[quantum number]] of [[hadron]]s determined by the number of [[charm quark]]s and [[antiquark]]s. #: {{cot|en|strangeness}} #* {{RQ:en:New York Times|author=Sandra Blakeslee|title=Another Particle Believed Discovered|date=1975-07-31|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1975/07/31/archives/another-particle-believed-discovered.html|passage=In trying to understand the long life of the psi particle, physicists postulated the notion of “'''charm'''.” '''Charm''', they say, prevents the “easy” decay of particles and thus prolongs their lifetimes. U particles, Dr. Pert said, may carry the property of '''charm'''.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20250812125414/https://www.nytimes.com/1975/07/31/archives/another-particle-believed-discovered.html|archivedate=12 August 2025}} # {{lb|en|finance}} A [[second-order]] measure of [[derivative]] price sensitivity, expressed as the instantaneous rate of change of [[delta]] with respect to time. #: {{syn|en|delta decay|DdeltaDtime}} #: {{hypernyms|en|Greeks}} # {{lb|en|GUI|Microsoft Windows}} An icon providing quick access to a command or setting. #* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=J. Peter Bruzzese|title=Using Windows 8 |passage=Undoubtedly one of the most important pieces to navigating Windows 8, '''charms''' are actually not visible until a command to show them is given.}} to allay; to soothe. #* {{RQ:Pope Works|volume=I|title=St. Cecilia's Day|canto=VII|page=378|passage=Music the fierceſt griefs can '''charm''', / And fate's ſevereſt rage diſarm: {{...}}}} =====Translations===== {{trans-top|seduce, entrance or fascinate}} * Armenian: * Bulgarian: * Danish: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hindi: * Hungarian: * Icelandic: * Ido: * Irish: * Latin: * Macedonian: * Māori: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|очаро́вывать|impf}}, {{t+|ru|очарова́ть|pf}}, {{t+|ru|оба́ивать|impf}}, {{t+|ru|обая́ть|pf}} * Spanish: * Turkish: {{trans-bottom}} {{trans-top|use a magical charm}} * Armenian: * Aromanian: * Azerbaijani: * Belarusian: * Bulgarian: * Catalan: * Dutch: * Esperanto: * Finnish: * French: * German: * Greek: * Hebrew: * Hungarian: * Kurdish: * Latin: * Luganda: * Macedonian: * Māori: * Polish: * Portuguese: * Romanian: * Russian: {{t+|ru|околдо́вывать|impf}}, {{t+|ru|околдова́ть|pf}};
